nh_huntington_ravine_winter_ice.blurb: Winter-only ice and mixed climbing in the glacial cirque on Mount Washington, reached by a long hike in from Pinkham Notch. Most of the fourteen climbs here are water-ice gullies, with a couple of mixed lines and one snow route. Grades cluster around WI3, with a few easier gullies below that and a handful of harder WI4 to WI5 pitches and moderate mixed climbs. The gullies run several pitches and are serious, committing terrain high on the mountain: weather, avalanche danger and icefall all matter, so check conditions first. It sees real traffic on midwinter weekends, drawing climbers from Boston, New York and Canada.

nh_5_lost_boys_area.blurb: A newly developed, steeper wing at the far right end of the big cliff on North Bald Cap, in New Hampshire's Great North Woods. The fourteen routes are mostly bolted sport lines with a few trad, and the difficulty is centered on 5.10, with a few easier lines from 5.7 to 5.9 and a small group of 5.11 and 5.12 routes. Holds and features are good, though the routes are young and some loose rock may remain. The wall is shorter than the slabs next door but much more upright, and some part of it is usually in shade. The path in is little used, so allow time and expect it to be overgrown.

nh_dome_the_2.blurb: A quiet, out-of-the-way crag at Pawtuckaway State Park in Nottingham, perched above the marsh that feeds Round Pond. It is mainly a top-roping spot, with sturdy trees on top for anchors and many variations possible off one rope, plus short trad lines and a few boulder problems. Most roped climbs are easy to moderate, mostly 5.5 to 5.7 with a couple near 5.9 and 5.10, and the problems run from V0 to V5. Because it sees less traffic than the park's main crags, the rock keeps better friction. It gets more sun and a breeze, so it dries fast and has fewer bugs. The trail up is faint and steep.

nh_lower_cliff.blurb: A small, seldom-visited trad cliff at Pawtuckaway State Park in Nottingham, set back behind the Trailside boulders by North Marsh. The fourteen routes are all traditional lines on cracks and roofs, up to roughly 60 feet at the tallest, running from easy 5.5 climbs through a solid middle of 5.7 to 5.10 and a single 5.11. The face catches sun for most of the day, but it can seep and run with water from the hillside above after rain. You will probably have it to yourself, though perhaps not to the spiders. Pawtuckaway is the state's southernmost major climbing area.
